Artillerijeger

Artillerijeger fitness requirements

Illustrative training photograph

SELECTION TEST

At a glance

The Norwegian Artillerijeger entry page lists an 8 km run with a 22 kg pack, alongside running, strength and swimming tests.

FEATURED ACTIVITY8 km pack run22 kg pack · 52 minutes

What the test includes

  • 8 km pack run with 22 kg in 52 minutes
  • 3,000 m run in 12 minutes 30 seconds
  • 30 push-ups and 6 pull-ups
  • Medicine-ball throw: 4.6 m; standing long jump: 2.25 m
  • 400 m swim

Some programmes include more than the activities listed here.

Test protocol and standards

These minimums apply to the published Artillerijeger education route requiring completed initial service. The initial-service route has separate requirements.

Official information checked 2026-11-24. Confirm current requirements with the test publisher.

EventPublished minimumPractice context
8 km pack run52:00 with 22 kgAverage 6:30 per km
3,000 m road run12:30Average 4:10 per km
Push-ups30Count approved repetitions
Pull-ups6Use the published technique
Medicine-ball throw4.6 mConfirm the prescribed setup
Standing long jump2.25 mMeasure from the start line
400 m swimPassNo numeric time published here

Scoring and scope

The education page identifies these as minimum physical requirements and warns that later training-stage tests differ. Do not treat the thresholds as a complete selection prediction.

  • Separate initial-service route

Before you rehearse the test

  1. Check whether you are preparing for initial service or the education route. Use the appropriate standards, not a mixture of both.
  2. Prepare the 8 km loaded effort and unloaded 3,000 m run separately first; practise the swimming component only in a supervised setting.

How to prepare

Independent training guidance, not official test instructions. Scale sessions to your current capacity and recover between demanding efforts.

  • Build running speed without a pack. Keep loaded endurance sessions predominantly controlled and build gradually from a manageable load.
  • Use measured routes to monitor pace; introduce varied terrain and reliable pack fit after building a base.
  • Maintain pulling, pushing, jumping and throwing work; schedule supervised swim practice separately.

Putting it into a training week

Build the ability to walk comfortably for longer periods before introducing the demanding pack-run pace. Keep most loaded sessions easy; use unloaded running to develop speed.

Common mistakes

  • Starting with a 22 kg pack because it is the test weight.
  • Confusing the education route with initial-service selection, or treating a single minimum result as readiness.

What to log

Record actual pack mass, distance, terrain, elapsed time, unloaded 3,000 m result and recovery.

Avoid repeated maximal tests and sudden load increases. Stop if pain, dizziness or unusual symptoms occur; use qualified supervision where appropriate.

Official test instructions

The organisation running the test is the best place to check the latest rules and requirements.

  • These figures come from the role’s published entry page. Other admission stages may use different distances and requirements.
  • Check the latest role page before making an application or setting a training target.
